newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials knocked lower, golds softer.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials knocked lower, golds softer.

text.p: South African industrial shares took a blow in mixed trading on Friday with dealers saying the index had been a victim of a sagging Dow Jones overnight, profit-taking and some poor economic data.
The industrial index also suffered from nervousness that world markets might slump after bearish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday, they said.
Greenspan warned that U.S. stock prices may have risen to too far and hinted that the Federal Reserve could hike U.S. interest rates.
South Africa's industrial index dropped 79.4 points to 8,244.3, the gold index ended down 22.6 points to 1,565.5 and the overall index lost 50.7 points to 7,145.3.
Golds stood soft for most of the day with dealers saying many market players did not believe the recent bullish trend in the bullion price could hold on for longer.
The yellow metal price shot through the psychologically important $360 per ounce level early on Friday, but by about 1447 GMT it had fallen back by about a dollar.
Dealers put Friday's volumes between 800 and 900 million rand.
They said the market was now awaiting Finance Minister Trevor Manuels's March 12 budget speech for direction.
Near-dated gold shares ended softer on the back of the slight fallback in the bullion price and the industrial contract was weaker on a poor Dow Jones on Thursday.
The March all-share contract was down at 6,485/500 from 6,578, the industrial contract slipped to 7,927/40 from 8,060 and the gold contract edged down to 1,100/08 from 1,125.
